analysis.title: US Capital Markets Perspectives, October 2026
key_insights: Federated Hermes projects 2026 global GDP growth of 3%. US Q2 2026 GDP grew 2.2% annualized. Growth is led by AI-related business investment, manufacturing and consumer spending.
Inflation is sticky and above the Fed's 2% target, sustained by high energy, freight and food costs. Disinflation needs energy prices to fall.
The Fed raised rates by 0.25% on September 16, 2026. FOMC members and markets anticipate further hikes. Inflation has overtaken the labor market as the immediate policy concern.
The September US jobs report was weaker than expected, but unemployment is low at 4.2%.
AI capex has fueled equity gains. Hyperscalers are issuing record debt in 2026, which competes with the Treasury market for buyers.
Since the start of the Iran war, the 10-year Treasury yield has risen 132 basis points to 5.29% as of 9/30/26. The 10-year term premium has also risen.
Real yields are rising because of resilient growth, heavy AI infrastructure capex and heavy government debt supply, which the report calls a structural repricing of rates.
Oil surpassed $100 per barrel after the Iran war began and has fluctuated around that level since. Central banks (ECB, BOJ, Fed) have begun raising rates. The BoE has held.
In Q1 2026, AI-related investment contributed 1.34 percentage points to the US economy's 2% growth. The report says the AI boom is still climbing in year three, when prior booms peaked and declined.

The report names four scenarios: resilient growth with slow disinflation, inflation persistence (stagflation lite), productivity-led growth, and a downside shock or hard landing, which it calls a tail risk.
Policy error becomes a risk if the Fed hikes more than markets expect, particularly if growth weakens under higher mortgage and variable-rate costs and falling sentiment.

The report recommends diversification beyond top-tier tech into international and emerging markets, US small caps and alternatives. It cites inflation, volatility, geopolitics and possible fiscal policy changes after the US mid-term elections as reasons.

macro_indicators.interpretation: IMF-based projection showing resilient global growth driven by AI investment and consumer spending.
Positive US growth, which the report says rules out stagflation as a near-term concern.
Federated Hermes forecast. Inflation is still above the Fed's target.
Federated Hermes forecast of slow disinflation.
Up 132 basis points since the start of the Iran war.
The labor market is still relatively strong despite a weaker than expected jobs report.
The Fed is in a tightening cycle, with more hikes expected by FOMC members and markets.

risk_factors: Policy error if the Fed hikes more than markets expect while growth weakens.
Surging mortgage and variable-rate costs, and falling sentiment, could weaken growth.
Higher interest rates are dampening housing, which could increasingly affect investment and spending.
A rapid shock could produce a downside or hard-landing scenario.
Energy prices stay high, which keeps inflation elevated and weighs on consumers.
Heavy hyperscaler debt issuance and government debt supply add pressure on Treasury yields.
Geopolitical conflict and possible fiscal policy changes after the US mid-term elections.
charts_described: Global GDP growth rates chart shows 2026 consensus estimates by region, including US 2.3%, China 4.6%, Eurozone 1.1%, Japan 0.6% and UK 1.2%.
US Treasury yield curve chart compares 2/27/26 with 9/30/26, with the 10-year at 5.29% on 9/30/26.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility has been a constant in bond markets. Treasury yields have been volatile on shifting Fed expectations and inflation concerns.
The report says markets have already priced in much of the further Fed tightening that recent inflation prints may support.
geopolitical: The Iran war began earlier in 2026 and pushed oil above $100 per barrel.
Energy supply shocks and ongoing geopolitical conflicts have stalled disinflation.
US mid-term elections may bring more pronounced trends and possible fiscal policy changes.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient growth and a slow disinflation path let the Fed tighten gradually, and markets have already priced in much of the tightening.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed could hike more than markets expect while mortgage and variable-rate costs surge and sentiment falls, which would weaken growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy prices staying high, which keeps inflation from easing, or the Fed hiking more than markets expect.

tension_points.bull_case: AI moves from buildout to adoption and lifts productivity, wages and profits, supported by strong household and hyperscaler balance sheets and ISM manufacturing above 52 all year.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher rates are dampening housing and growth is softening, which could spread to investment and spending.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rapid downside shock that spreads to investment and spending.
